id: qc-08
title: Below-threshold error correction
paper: Google Quantum AI, Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold (arXiv Aug 2024; Nature 638, 920, 2025)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.13687
type: Replication
cutoff: 2024-08-24
domain: qc
profile: hardware-milestone

## expected_verdict
Supported (scoped), tier C. Exponential suppression of logical memory error with distance (Λ = 2.14 ± 0.02 from d = 3 → 5 → 7), beyond break-even by 2.4×, with a real-time decoder at d = 5. This is a quantum memory result: not logical gates, not full fault tolerance. No independent replication of the same claim on another platform found yet.

## I0
Does logical error decrease as surface-code distance increases under a fixed operating regime?

## evidence
- Hardware: 105-qubit superconducting processor (distance-7 surface code, 101 qubits incl. leakage-removal qubits); a 72-qubit processor for d = 5 with a real-time decoder.
- Headline: Λ = 2.14 ± 0.02 (neural-network decoder); Λ = 2.04 ± 0.02 with ensembled matching; d = 7 logical error 0.143% ± 0.003% per cycle; simulation predicts Λ_sim = 2.25.
- Beyond break-even: d = 7 logical lifetime exceeds the best physical qubit by 2.4 ± 0.3.
- Real time: average decoder latency 63 µs at d = 5 for up to 10⁶ cycles; cycle time 1.1 µs.
- Limits: repetition codes up to d = 29 hit an error floor ~10⁻¹⁰ from rare correlated bursts ~once per hour (~3×10⁹ cycles); data-qubit leakage removal (DQLR) used every cycle.
- Authors: "if scaled, could realize" fault-tolerant requirements; <10⁻¹⁰ needed for many algorithms.

## intake
- Scope: surface-code memory below threshold: ε_d falls by Λ per distance step d → d+2, at d = 3, 5, 7.
- Regime: memory experiments (no logical operations), ~250 cycles typical for Λ fits; superconducting transmons; offline best decoders for Λ, real-time decoder at d = 5.
- Assumptions: detection probabilities stable across the run; decoders comparable across distances; correlated errors rare relative to experiment length.
- Falsifiers: Λ ≤ 1 with matched decoders and cycle definitions; correlated bursts dominating at larger d; break-even claim depending on decoder choice.

## screen
- Must flag: Λ depends on decoder (2.14 NN vs 2.04 matching); memory only; correlated error floor; leakage-removal overhead counts toward qubit cost.
- Must request: Λ with the real-time decoder at d = 7; logical gate results; independent replication.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Google 2023 "Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a surface code logical qubit" (d = 3 vs 5, Λ ≈ 1); Fowler et al. 2012 surface code; Google 2021 exponential suppression of bit-flip errors with repetition codes; Bluvstein et al. 2023 neutral-atom logical processor; neural-network decoders (Bausch et al.).
- Current mode: no independent same-claim replication in inventory.

## designer
- Fix decoder and cycle definitions across d; pre-register Λ fit method; include long runs to measure burst rates; separate memory from logical-operation claims.

## champion
- The best physical qubit (break-even reference) and the d = 3 code; for decoding, ensembled matching as the reference decoder.

## panel
- Accept with scope: "memory below threshold"; request decoder-matched Λ and burst statistics in the main claims.

## run
- Stim + PyMatching simulation of a d = 3/5/7 surface code memory at the reported physical error rates; check Λ_sim ≈ 2.25. Hardware data: recompute Λ from released detection events if available.

## verdict
- Label: Supported (scoped), tier C.
- Must say: exponential suppression demonstrated for memory; fault tolerance for computation not shown; no independent replication.
- Must not say: fault-tolerant quantum computing achieved; or the result is replicated.

## audit
- Check: Λ = 2.14 ± 0.02; 0.143% per cycle; 2.4 ± 0.3 break-even; 63 µs latency; 1.1 µs cycle; d = 29 repetition codes; ~1 burst/hour.

## variants
- Longer runs (hours) at d = 7 to quantify bursts; logical gates between below-threshold patches; replication on another platform.
